All exact price/indicator claims below are anchored to the **verified market snapshot** (source of truth). The individual indicator feeds matched the snapshot on every overlapping value (50 SMA 178.09, 200 SMA 177.26, 10 EMA 155.60, RSI 36.06, MACD −9.11, MACD histogram −3.15, Bollinger lower band 141.11, ATR 10.44) — no material discrepancies. One cosmetic note: the RSI feed contained a few garbled/misaligned rows in early August (e.g., a broken date token `026-08-09`); the key recent values are consistent with the snapshot, so nothing is reconciled or invented here.

---

## 1. Indicator Selection Rationale (8 indicators, complementary, non-redundant)

| Slot | Indicator | Why chosen for this tape |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **close_200_sma** | Long-term regime filter. COIN is testing a potential regime line; the 200-day defines strategic bias. |
| 2 | **close_50_sma** | Medium-term trend + 50/200 spread (death-cross context), which is live and actionable here. |

| 4 | **macd** | Medium-term momentum. Currently at its most extreme reading of the entire 90-day lookback — a primary trend-momentum gauge. |
| 5 | **macdh** | Earliest deceleration detector. First histogram uptick after a waterfall is the classic early reversal tell; `macd` alone can't show that. |
| 6 | **rsi** | Sole momentum oscillator. Tapped its lowest reading of the window (29.70 on 11/2) — oversold context for the bounce. (StochRSI deliberately excluded to avoid redundancy.) |

**Deliberately excluded:** `macds` (fully redundant — MACD line vs. signal spread is exactly the histogram), `boll`/`boll_ub` (lower band is the operative boundary in a breakdown; snapshot supplies the rest), `vwma` (volume read taken directly from raw OHLCV; avoids a third redundant average).

## 3. Multi-Phase Trend Structure (from raw OHLCV, all dates/prices tool-sourced)

1. **April–May: broad range, 180–216.** Close 172.99 (4/1) → rally to 211.63 (4/20) → May 11 close 216.60, May 14 intraday high 222.35 → fade to ~180 by month-end.
2. **June: breakdown leg.** June 5 close 152.40; June 25 close 142.52 (intraday low 141.48); month-end close 146.19 (6/30).
3. **July: failed repair.** Rebound to 175.85 (7/21), then a **−10.6% single-session collapse on 7/31** (163.58 → 146.26) on **20.87M shares** — one of two ~10.6% crash days in the window.
4. **August: violent base-and-breakout.** Base 141–154 (8/3–8/18), then **+27.5% in three sessions** (close 146.23 on 8/18 → 186.49 on 8/21) on escalating volume (16.96M / 17.57M / **22.74M** — the window's biggest day, an up day).
5. **September: recovery top.** Advance to closes 201.05/201.07 (9/21–9/22), intraday window top **208.33** (9/21); distribution drift begins 9/23.
6. **October: staircase breakdown.** Sequence of lower closes: 183.00 (10/2) → 172.00 (10/8) → 168.45 (10/19) → 164.45 (10/23) → 159.60 (10/26) → **143.54 on 10/30 (−10.6%, 20.89M shares)** → **137.83 on 11/2 (low 135.46)** — the lowest print of the entire 7-month window.
7. **11/3: relief bounce.** Close 145.45 (**+5.5%** vs. 11/2), intraday swing from 137.89 to 150.51, closing in the upper half of the range — but leaving a 5.1-point upper wick (supply into strength).

**Net geometry:** From the 9/21 high (208.33) to the 11/2 low (135.46): **−35.0%**. From the May high (222.35): **−39.0%**. From the first window close (172.99): **−15.9%**. The August–September recovery has been fully round-tripped and then some.

---

## 4. Moving Averages — Bearish Stack, With a Subtle Death-Cross Nuance

- **All three averages are above price and falling** (200 SMA 177.26 > 50 SMA 178.09 are nearly coincident; 10 EMA 155.60). Price sits **−6.5%** below the 10 EMA, **−18.3%** below the 50 SMA, and **−17.9%** below the 200 SMA. That's deep, extended dislocation — bearish regime, but stretched.
- **The 50/200 spread has been negative for the entire retrieved window** (e.g., 8/5: 161.90 vs 209.63; 9/21: 167.50 vs 188.91) — i.e., the market has been in a death-cross state since before early August.
- **Nuance worth flagging:** the 50 SMA briefly popped marginally **above** the 200 SMA from 10/27 through 11/3 (gap of only **+0.82** on 11/3: 178.09 vs 177.26). This is largely a **window-roll artifact** — early-August lows (~145–150) rolling out of the 50-day window while late-April/May prints (~180–190) roll in — not a trend repair. With price 32+ points below both lines, the 50 SMA (−0.68 on 11/2, −0.68 on 11/3) is resuming its decline relative to the 200 SMA (−0.51/day). **Expect the spread to re-widen negative imminently** unless price reclaims ~177–178 quickly. Treat any near-term "golden-cross" headline with skepticism.

---

## 5. Momentum — Maximum Stress, First Flicker of Deceleration

- **MACD: −9.11 (11/3)** — the **most negative reading of the entire 90-day lookback** (window range roughly +7.64 on 8/31 to −9.11 now; the prior worst was ~−3.9 in mid-August). The line is still falling (−8.58 → −9.11 day-over-day) and sits 3.15 points below its signal (−5.96). No bullish cross exists; medium-term momentum is at maximum recorded stress.
- **MACD Histogram: −3.15 (11/3) vs −3.41 (11/2)** — the **first uptick since 10/29** (prior sequence: −1.84 → −2.69 → −3.41). This is the earliest, weakest possible signal that downside momentum is decelerating. It is *not* a reversal signal on its own — the histogram is still deeply negative — but it typically precedes the MACD line curling.
- **RSI: 36.06 (11/3)**, rebounding from **29.70 (11/2)** — the **lowest RSI in the 90-day lookback** (window high was 66.96 on 8/21). The 11/2 print was a genuine touch of the oversold zone (sub-30); the reclaim above 30 on 11/3 accompanied the +5.5% close. Note: on closes there is **no clean bullish divergence** (11/2's low 135.46 undercut 10/30's 136.89 *and* RSI was lower, 29.70 vs 31.91), so the bounce rests on oversold reversion, not divergence — a weaker evidentiary basis.

**Momentum verdict:** trend still fully bearish; oversold snapback in progress; confirmation requires the MACD line to flatten and cross its signal, which given the −3.15 gap will take several sessions even in a strong bounce.

---

## 6. Volatility & Mean Reversion — Bands Stretched to the Edge

- **Bollinger (20, 2σ):** middle **167.11**, lower **141.11**, upper **193.11** — a **52-point band (~31% of the middle)**, the widest of the window, mechanically swollen by October's collapse.
- **Band events:** COIN closed **below the lower band two consecutive sessions** — 143.54 vs 149.81 (10/30) and 137.83 vs 143.96 (11/2) — then **re-entered the band on 11/3** (145.45 > 141.11). Price remains pinned at the very bottom of the band structure (%B ≈ 8%). Close-back-below-141.11 would negate the reversion attempt; a push toward the 167.11 middle band is the standard mean-reversion magnet if the bounce extends.
- **ATR: 10.44** — 7.2% of the current close, versus ~6.3% relative ATR at the 9/21 top (12.68 vs 201.05). Absolute ATR is below its September peak, but **relative volatility is the highest of the window** — the tape is moving violently on a smaller price base. Practical consequence: stops must be wide (1.5–2.0 ATR ≈ **15.7–20.9 points**, i.e., roughly the 129.7–124.6 zone from the current close), and position sizes should be cut proportionally. Single sessions of ±5.5% to ±10.6% (11/3, 7/31, 10/30) are the norm, not the exception, right now.

---

## 7. Volume Structure — Capitulation Signature, Unconfirmed Bounce

- Typical baseline volume is **5–9M**; event days run **14–23M**. Every structural turn in the window came on a volume spike: 7/31 crash (20.87M), 8/19–8/21 breakout (17.0M / 17.6M / **22.74M**), 9/18 thrust (21.92M), and the **10/30 capitulation (20.89M)** — the second-largest down-day volume of the window.
- The 11/2 flush (10.64M) was lighter than 10/30 — consistent with exhausting supply — and the 11/3 bounce (10.59M) is **roughly baseline-plus, not surge-level**. Verdict: **downside capitulation is plausible but the bounce is unconfirmed by volume**. A reclaim of 155–160 on >14–15M shares would materially strengthen the reversal case; without it, treat the 11/3 pop as a bear-market rally candidate.

---

## 8. Key Levels (all tool-sourced, dated)

**Support:**
- **135.46** (11/2 low) / **137.89** (11/3 low) — the operative floor; a daily close below 135.46 breaks the lowest print of the 7-month window and opens uncharted-down territory (psychological 130 / 125).
- **139.11–141.48** (7/31 and 6/25 lows) — now *overhead-less*; this June–July shelf has been undercut, flipping it into a first resistance pocket.
- **141.11** — Bollinger lower band (dynamic).

**Resistance:**
- **150.51** (11/3 high) — first test; the 5.1-point upper wick shows sellers appeared there.
- **155.60** (10 EMA) — falling ~2.2/day; the key short-term battleground.
- **159.60–163.26** (10/26–10/29 closes) — prior congestion that broke down.
- **167.11** (Bollinger middle) / **168.45–177.08** (10/19–10/21 closes) — the heavy mid-October supply band.
- **177.26–178.09** (200 SMA / 50 SMA) — regime line; reclaiming this negates the death-cross regime entirely.

---

## 9. Scenario Framework & Actionable Guidance

**Primary (bearish continuation, base case):** Price below all three MAs, MACD at record-negative extremes, 50/200 spread about to re-widen negative. Rallies toward **155–160** are supply zones. Below **135.46**, continuation targets are psychological rather than technical (130 / 125); with ATR 10.4, expect the move to happen in 2–3 violent sessions, not a glide path.

**Tactical bull (oversold snapback, active now):** RSI reclaim from sub-30 (29.70 → 36.06), histogram first uptick, lower-band re-entry, +5.5% close, and 10/30 capitulation volume collectively justify *limited* long exposure for mean-reversion traders. Structure: entries near **143–146**; invalidation = daily close **< 135.46** (~1.0–1.1 ATR of risk); targets **155.60** (10 EMA) → **159.6–163** → stretch **167.11**. Risk/reward ≈ 1:1.3 to first target, ~1:2+ to the middle band. **Size down hard** — this is a falling-knife bounce until proven otherwise.

**Confirmation triggers to flip constructive:**
1. Daily close **> 155.60** with the MACD line crossing above its signal (−5.96 and rising);
2. Close **> 167.11** to negate the short-term downtrend;
3. Close **> 177–178** to negate the long-term (50/200) downtrend — a tall order given the current 32-point deficit.

**What I cannot certify from tools:** fundamental/news drivers of the 10/30 gap-down, options positioning, and any claim of *historical* support/resistance "bounces" beyond the dated levels listed. All price/indicator numbers above are directly tool-verified for their stated dates.

Treat longs as tactical (targets 155.60 → 163 → 167.11, stop below 135.46, ATR-adjusted size); treat the 135.46/141.11 zone as the line between "snapback" and "new leg down."
